sequence_based_measurement.abstract_quote: We describe Cleavage Under Targets and Release Using Nuclease (CUT&RUN), a chromatin profiling strategy in which antibody-targeted controlled cleavage by micrococcal nuclease releases specific protein-DNA complexes into the supernatant for paired-end DNA sequencing.
sequence_based_measurement.rationale: Targeted enzymatic cleavage physically releases protein-DNA complexes for sequencing, establishing a sequence-based experimental measurement workflow. Detailed library-preparation steps are not supplied.

assay_workflow_contribution.abstract_quote: Unlike Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP), which fragments and solubilizes total chromatin, CUT&RUN is performed in situ, allowing for both quantitative high-resolution chromatin mapping and probing of the local chromatin environment.
assay_workflow_contribution.rationale: The in situ targeted cleavage-and-release strategy establishes an assay-level measurement architecture. The abstract describes its operating principle without providing a complete protocol.

experimental_demonstration.abstract_quote: When applied to yeast and human nuclei, CUT&RUN yielded precise transcription factor profiles while avoiding crosslinking and solubilization issues.
experimental_demonstration.rationale: Reported profiles from yeast and human nuclei establish experimental assay demonstration. Detailed validation data and replicate counts are not presented in the abstract.

papers.rationale: CUT&RUN contributes a physical sequencing-based chromatin-profiling workflow and demonstrates its experimental performance, satisfying all three criteria.

sequence_based_measurement.abstract_quote: Here we developed simultaneous high-throughput ATAC and RNA expression with sequencing (SHARE-seq), a highly scalable approach for measurement of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same single cell, applicable to different tissues.
sequence_based_measurement.rationale: The abstract explicitly describes sequencing-based measurement of accessibility and RNA in the same cell. The molecular capture and library-construction steps are unspecified.

assay_workflow_contribution.abstract_quote: Here we developed simultaneous high-throughput ATAC and RNA expression with sequencing (SHARE-seq), a highly scalable approach for measurement of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same single cell, applicable to different tissues.
assay_workflow_contribution.rationale: Development of a platform for joint same-cell measurements establishes an assay architecture contribution. Its implementation details are not provided in the abstract.

experimental_demonstration.abstract_quote: Using 34,774 joint profiles from mouse skin, we develop a computational strategy to identify cis-regulatory interactions and define domains of regulatory chromatin (DORCs) that significantly overlap with super-enhancers.
experimental_demonstration.rationale: The mouse-skin joint profiles support experimental deployment of the described assay. Subsequent computational analysis does not itself establish technical performance benchmarks.

papers.rationale: SHARE-seq introduces and experimentally deploys a joint single-cell sequencing assay; the accompanying computational and biological findings do not diminish that contribution.

sequence_based_measurement.abstract_quote: We also observe higher library diversity generated by Tn5-059 when compared to Nextera v2 for human exomes, which leads to less sequencing and lower cost per genome.
sequence_based_measurement.rationale: Sequencing-library generation and comparison for human exomes establish a physical sequencing-library workflow. The reaction protocol is not detailed.

assay_workflow_contribution.abstract_quote: We demonstrate Tn5-059 reduces AT dropout and increases uniformity of genome coverage in both bacterial genomes and human genome. We also observe higher library diversity generated by Tn5-059 when compared to Nextera v2 for human exomes, which leads to less sequencing and lower cost per genome.
assay_workflow_contribution.rationale: Measured improvements in coverage and library diversity establish an experimentally improved library-preparation workflow beyond the discovery of an engineered reagent. A wholly new measurement architecture is not established or required.

experimental_demonstration.abstract_quote: In addition, when used for human exomes, Tn5-059 delivers consistent library insert size over a range of input DNA, allowing up to a tenfold variance from the 50 ng input recommendation.
experimental_demonstration.rationale: Library insert-size results across DNA inputs demonstrate experimental workflow testing. The abstract does not provide the complete experimental design.

papers.rationale: The engineered transposase is demonstrated to improve sequencing-library performance, satisfying the assay-workflow improvement criterion rather than supporting only a component contribution.

sequence_based_measurement.abstract_quote: We developed chromVAR (http://www.github.com/GreenleafLab/chromVAR), an R package for analyzing sparse chromatin-accessibility data by estimating gain or loss of accessibility within peaks sharing the same motif or annotation while controlling for technical biases.
sequence_based_measurement.rationale: The reported method computationally analyzes existing accessibility measurements. Its sequencing-data inputs do not establish a physical measurement workflow performed or introduced here.

assay_workflow_contribution.abstract_quote: We developed chromVAR (http://www.github.com/GreenleafLab/chromVAR), an R package for analyzing sparse chromatin-accessibility data by estimating gain or loss of accessibility within peaks sharing the same motif or annotation while controlling for technical biases.
assay_workflow_contribution.rationale: The contribution is an analysis package that estimates accessibility variation and controls computational biases. No physical assay or library-preparation modification is reported.

experimental_demonstration.abstract_quote: chromVAR enables accurate clustering of scATAC-seq profiles and characterization of known and de novo sequence motifs associated with variation in chromatin accessibility.
experimental_demonstration.rationale: The stated results concern computational clustering and motif analysis. They do not demonstrate a new or improved physical assay experimentally.

papers.rationale: This is an original computational methods contribution, supporting a primary_methods publication role and software_only classification.

sequence_based_measurement.rationale: ChIP-seq validation explicitly establishes a physical sequencing-based measurement. The workflows used for the matched epigenome and transcriptome measurements are not specified.

assay_workflow_contribution.abstract_quote: We generated matched epigenome and transcriptome measurements in 86 primary cell types that span the mouse immune system and its differentiation cascades.
assay_workflow_contribution.rationale: Matched data generation is explicit, but the abstract does not state whether it involved a new assay architecture or experimentally improved preparation workflow. An assay-level contribution cannot be established from this passage.

experimental_demonstration.abstract_quote: We generated matched epigenome and transcriptome measurements in 86 primary cell types that span the mouse immune system and its differentiation cascades.
experimental_demonstration.rationale: Generated measurements across primary cell types establish completed experimental work. The abstract does not establish that these experiments demonstrate a technical workflow innovation.

papers.rationale: The abstract establishes experimental sequencing measurements and biological analyses, but leaves an assay-level contribution unspecified. This uncertainty prevents a definitive assay or application judgment.
papers.focused_question: Do the Methods and validation figures describe a new or improved physical assay or library-preparation workflow for the matched epigenome and transcriptome measurements, and which experimental comparison demonstrates that contribution?

sequence_based_measurement.abstract_quote: Here, we present simple and robust procedures for Tn5 transposase production and optimized reaction conditions for tagmentation-based sequencing library construction.
sequence_based_measurement.rationale: The procedures explicitly include physical construction of sequencing libraries by tagmentation. Downstream sequencing settings are not described.

assay_workflow_contribution.abstract_quote: We further show how molecular crowding agents both modulate library lengths and enable efficient tagmentation from subpicogram amounts of cDNA.
assay_workflow_contribution.rationale: Demonstrated control of library length and efficient low-input tagmentation establish a library-preparation improvement. The contribution includes reaction optimization, while detailed conditions are absent from the abstract.

experimental_demonstration.abstract_quote: The comparison of single-cell RNA-sequencing libraries generated using produced and commercial Tn5 demonstrated equal performances in terms of gene detection and library characteristics.
experimental_demonstration.rationale: Generated single-cell RNA-sequencing libraries and measured performance comparisons establish experimental validation. This comparison alone demonstrates equivalence; the separate crowding-agent results establish workflow improvement.

papers.rationale: Optimized tagmentation conditions and experimentally demonstrated library-preparation capabilities satisfy all three criteria, with a contribution extending beyond transposase production.

sequence_based_measurement.abstract_quote: scNMT-seq (single-cell nucleosome, methylation and transcription sequencing) uses a GpC methyltransferase to label open chromatin followed by bisulfite and RNA sequencing.
sequence_based_measurement.rationale: Physical enzymatic chromatin labeling is read out through bisulfite and RNA sequencing. Complete library-preparation details are not supplied.

assay_workflow_contribution.abstract_quote: Here, we report a single-cell method for parallel chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation and transcriptome profiling.
assay_workflow_contribution.rationale: A single-cell workflow combining three molecular measurements establishes an assay architecture contribution. Detailed integration steps are not described in the abstract.

experimental_demonstration.abstract_quote: We validate scNMT-seq by applying it to differentiating mouse embryonic stem cells, finding links between all three molecular layers and revealing dynamic coupling between epigenomic layers during differentiation.
experimental_demonstration.rationale: Application to differentiating cells with results across all three molecular layers explicitly demonstrates the assay experimentally. Quantitative technical benchmarks are not presented.

papers.rationale: scNMT-seq introduces a physical joint sequencing assay and validates it in biological samples, satisfying all three criteria.
